Assignments are distributed and collected through **GitHub**. For each homework
you get your own **private repository** in the course organization, and
**pushing to that repository is how you submit**. There is no separate submit
step and no upload form.

## Register your GitHub username (once)

Everything below depends on us knowing your GitHub handle, so do this first.

1. If you don't already have a GitHub account, create one at
   [github.com/join](https://github.com/join).
2. Submit your name, email, and GitHub **username** in the form below. Your
   username is the part after `github.com/` when you visit your own profile,
   not your display name.

## How to submit a homework

1. **Accept your repository invite.** When a homework is released, we create a
   private repo named `hwN-<your-github-username>` in the course organization
   and add you to it. GitHub emails you an invitation (it also appears at
   [github.com/notifications](https://github.com/notifications)). Make sure to **accept it**,
   or you won't be able to push. Invites expire after 7 days; email me if yours lapses.
2. **Clone your repo and set up the Julia environment:**
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/uw-econ-bootcamp-2026/hwN-<your-github-username>.git
   cd hwN-<your-github-username>
   ```
   ```julia
   julia> ]              # enter package mode
   (@v1) pkg> activate .
   (HomeworkN) pkg> instantiate
   ```
3. **Write your answers in `homeworkN.jl`.** How you organize the file is up to
   you, but keep the exact function names and signatures the prompt
   specifies — they are listed in the PDF and in your repo's `README.md`.
4. **Run the local smoke tests before you push:**
   ```bash
   julia --project=. test/runtests.jl
   ```
   These check that your functions exist with the right names and arities; they
   do not check whether your answers are correct. They catch the single most
   common way an otherwise-correct assignment loses points.
5. **Push to submit:**
   ```bash
   git add -A
   git commit -m "Submit homework N"
   git push
   ```
   Your latest pushed commit is what gets graded. You can push as many times as
   you like before the due date; due dates for every assignment are listed on the
   [Homeworks](homeworks.qmd) page.

## How you get feedback

Grading scripts run periodically. Each run
pulls the latest commit from your repo, runs a test suite against your
functions, and posts a report back to your repo as a GitHub issue titled
*"Homework N — feedback"* — GitHub emails you when it appears.

**Those automated checks are a first pass, not your grade.** A report labelled
*provisional* tells you what the machine could and couldn't verify; use it to
catch problems before the deadline. I read every submission myself and post your
actual grade, with comments, in the same issue thread.

If a provisional report looks wrong, it usually points at something concrete:

- **`UndefVarError: <name> not defined`** — a function is named differently from
  what the prompt requires. Rename it to fix.
- **"could not be loaded"** — `homeworkN.jl` has a syntax error, or a `using`
  for a package that isn't in `Project.toml`.
- **"did not finish"** — an infinite loop, or slow top-level code that runs on
  load. 

Email me if you're stuck on any of these.
